title: Lowe's (LOW) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
transcript:
Online and Pro gains offset fuel-cost pressure this quarter.

ByMotley Fool Transcribing–Nov 18, 2026 at 2:56PM EST

DATE

Wed, Nov. 18, 2026

CALL PARTICIPANTS

TAKEAWAYS

RISKS

SUMMARY

Lowe's(LOW+0.45%)reported growth across its strategic priorities, including Pro, online, and home services, despite facing broader macroeconomic challenges. Management reported that the company achieved its sixth consecutive quarter of positive comparable sales, supported by strong performance in essential replacement categories and digital channels. The company is integrating its recent acquisitions of Foundation Building Materials and Artisan Design Group to expand its reach into the commercial and Pro distribution markets. Management stated it remains focused on its Total Home Strategy and Perpetual Productivity Improvement initiatives to manage external cost pressures such as fuel and transportation. The company updated its full-year guidance to reflect third-quarter execution while maintaining a disciplined approach to capital allocation through dividends and investments in fulfillment infrastructure.

Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator:Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Lowe's Companies third quarter 2026 earnings conference call. My name is Rob, and I'll be your operator for today's call. Just a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I'll now turn the call over to Shelly Hubbard, Vice President of Investor Relations.

Shelly Hubbard:Thank you and good morning. Here with me today are Marvin Ellison, Chairman, President, and Chief Executive Officer; Bill Boltz, our Executive Vice President, Merchandising; Quonta Vance, our Executive Vice President, Stores; and Brandon Sink, our Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. I would like to remind you that our notice regarding forward-looking statements is included in our press release this morning, which can be found on Lowe's Investor Relations website. During this call, we will be making comments that are forward-looking, including our expectations for fiscal 2026.

Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied as a result of various risks, uncertainties, and important factors, including those discussed in the risk factors, MD&A, and other sections of our annual report on Form 10-K and our other SEC filings. Additionally, we'll be discussing certain non-GAAP financial measures. A reconciliation of these items to U.S. GAAP can be found on the quarterly earnings section of our Investor Relations website. Now, I'll turn the call over to Marvin.

Marvin Ellison:Thank you, Shelly. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Third quarter sales were $22.8 billion, up 9.3%, and comparable sales increased 1.8%, driven by strong execution across the business. Our teams continue to prove that we're one of the best-executing retailers in the world, and our success during key selling events, including Labor Day, demonstrated the advantage of our scale and our ability to deliver value for customers in the current macro environment. In fact, this quarter marks the sixth consecutive quarter of positive sales comps. Additionally, investments we've made in our Total Home Strategy are continuing to drive results, particularly in Pro, online, and home services.

We also delivered growth in appliances, powered by our expansive fulfillment ecosystem that remains a key competitive advantage for us. These results reinforce our confidence in the resilience of our operating model and our ability to grow the business across different economic backdrops. Let me share more details about our performance this quarter. We delivered another quarter of Pro growth, supported by the investments we continue to make in the customer experience. Our small to medium-sized Pro customers continue to respond to the enhancements we have made to our fulfillment and loyalty offerings, helping us deepen those relationships and capture more of their spend.

We also delivered continued growth in home services this quarter, as investments we have made to improve the customer journey are resonating with our customers. Turning to our recent acquisitions. We are pleased with the progress we are making to integrate FBM and ADG, including putting FBM's fulfillment assets to work for Lowe's and introducing complementary Lowe's products to FBM customers. We are also seeing continued momentum across FBM's commercial business, as demonstrated by their recent work with the Jacksonville Jaguars to furnish and install exterior and interior doors for their stadium of the future. This project reflects how FBM is leveraging Lowe's relationship as an official NFL sponsor to grow their commercial business.

We look forward to sharing more about the integration of FBM and ADG in a few weeks at our analyst and investor conference. Let me turn to online. We delivered 17.4% growth in online sales this quarter, as both DIY and Pro customers continue to engage with Lowe's across our digital channels, as well as our stores. This marks the fifth consecutive quarter of double-digit online growth and the third straight quarter of online growth above 15%. Our continued online growth has been supported by the investments we made in fulfillment, giving customers more flexibility in how and when they receive their products. That brings me to the tariff refunds we received during the quarter.

As I have said before, we thought first about how we are going to share these refunds with the customer. Our intention is to reinvest our tariff refunds in ways that strengthen our customer value proposition by putting these dollars to work to enhance the customer experience, strengthen our competitive position, and bring value to our customers. Brandon will discuss our tariff refund reinvestment philosophy in more detail during the call. Lastly, I'd like to thank our frontline associates for their continued dedication to serving our customers regardless of the economic conditions, and we will remain focused on strong execution, disciplined investments, and delivering value for our customers and our shareholders.

We are excited to share more on December 9th at our analyst and investor conference, where we will discuss our evolving Total Home Strategy and how Lowe's is positioned to grow regardless of the market conditions. Before I turn over to Bill, I'd like to thank him for his eight years of outstanding service and leadership as our EVP of Merchandising. To say that Bill's work leading merchandising at Lowe's has been transformational would be an understatement. Bill was actually the first person I called when I accepted the CEO role at Lowe's in 2018, and our partnership over the past eight years has been truly outstanding.

We are pleased that Bill will remain with us through the end of the calendar year to support Margi's transition into her role as EVP of Merchandising. We're also delighted, beginning in 2027, Bill will serve as president of the Lowe's Foundation, a role that reflects his deep passion for giving back and his love for the company. I also want to congratulate Margi on her expanded role. Throughout her tenure at Lowe's, Margi has been a proven leader and delivered exceptional results across a variety of roles.

Margi's background as a former GMM and SVP of Home Decor and Hardlines, in addition to her nearly three years of leading the Lowe's supply chain, perfectly positions her for this new assignment as EVP of Merchandising. With that, let me turn the call over to Bill.

Bill Boltz:Thanks, Marvin, and good morning, everyone. It has been a privilege and an honor to lead the Lowe's merchandising team for the past eight years. I'm excited to hand the reins over to Margi to continue to deliver for our customers and our shareholders. As Marvin mentioned, I'm very passionate about our Lowe's Foundation, and I'm equally thrilled to take the role as president of the Lowe's Foundation in 2027. I look forward to working side by side with Margi for the balance of 2026 to ensure that she makes a seamless transition into her new role.

This quarter, our comp sales increased 1.8% with growth across building products, home decor, and hardlines, including positive comp sales in seven of our 13 merchandise divisions. That performance reflects our continued focus on what matters most to our customers: compelling value, leading brands, innovative products, and an easy shopping experience both in our stores and online. Turning first to building products. We delivered positive comp sales in electrical, lumber, and rough plumbing, reflecting our continued investments in the Pro. These include improved inventory breadth and depth, enhanced digital tools for customers and associates, and stronger service levels which help pros get in, get what they need, and get back to the job site faster.

In electrical, our growth went beyond just commodity categories, with positive comps in switchgear, wiring devices, as well as tools and attachments. We're continuing to strengthen Lowe's position as a destination for trade professionals, supported by trusted brands like Klein Tools, Southwire, and Eaton. We also delivered positive comps in rough plumbing, with broad-based growth led by HVAC, water heaters, pumps, irrigation, pipe and fittings, and air circulation. We're continuing to work with SharkBite on a multi-year strategy to bring new solutions to the Pro, including the new PEX Press System, which is exclusive to Lowe's in the home center channel.

This innovation gives pros a faster, simpler, and more cost-effective way to complete plumbing projects with a press-to-connect system that can cut installation time in half compared to a traditional crimp fitting. Now let's shift to home decor, where appliances was once again a standout, with positive comps for the eighth consecutive quarter. During our Labor Day event, we showcased the total value of an appliance purchase at Lowe's with an exclusive all-in offer for MyLowe's Rewards members that included delivery, haul-away, basic installation, and an extended warranty. This helped us drive strong appliance demand as we moved into the fall.

Our performance reflects the investments we have made in our fulfillment capabilities, along with our customer experience, both in-store and online. As a reminder, Lowe's also offers the broadest assortment of leading appliance brands and models, and that is an important distinction. Lowe's competitive advantage is our ability to combine speed with choice. We remain the only retailer in the U.S. who can deliver and hook up a wide range of major appliances same day and next day in virtually every zip code. We continue to give customers new reasons to trade up for innovation. One example is Whirlpool's new counter-depth French door refrigerator with the industry's first indoor nugget ice maker.

It gives customers the popular soft, chewable nugget ice, along with the traditional cubed ice in the freezer, so that they can have both options without needing a separate ice maker. Now turning to hardlines, where we delivered positive comp sales in power equipment, tools and hardware, and seasonal and cleaning, supported by new product innovation, strong brands, and great execution. In outdoor power equipment, our new DeWalt generators were popular with Pro customers, and both Pro and DIY customers responded to our industry-leading lineup, including John Deere, Toro, EGO, and Craftsman. In fact, many of our key brands delivered double-digit growth this quarter, and our strong in-stocks helped us meet customer demand throughout the season.

In power tools, we delivered strength across our major cordless platforms as we continue to bring customers the latest innovation from leading brands like DeWalt, Bosch, Metabo, Kobalt, and Craftsman. One great innovation for the Pro is the new Metabo HPT Gen3 Cordless Nailer, which is now available in all of our stores exclusively at Lowe's within the home center channel. It combines the convenience of cordless with the power pros expect from a pneumatic nailer without having to deal with the compressor or hose. It is fast, lightweight, and designed to deliver more shots per charge, helping pros work more efficiently.

This quarter, we are adding even more depth to our power tools assortment with an expanded lineup of nailers from DeWalt, giving Lowe's the largest assortment of DeWalt power tools and accessories of any U.S. home improvement retailer. We are also continuing to strengthen our private brand power tools assortment with the largest new product introduction in Kobalt history, including 20 new 24-volt power tools. This launch also introduces our new TXP tabless battery technology, which delivers up to 40% more power in a smaller package while remaining compatible with the Kobalt 24-volt tools our customers already own.

Kobalt is a great example of how our own brands can deliver innovation and performance while providing a compelling value for our customers. As we look ahead to Black Friday, we are excited about our Trim-A-Tree set and our gift zone, along with the strong offers planned across key categories, highlighting the value, brands, and innovation that customers expect from Lowe's. As I close, we are pleased with the growth we delivered across all three of our merchandising areas this quarter. We remain focused on building on that performance by giving our customers compelling assortments with compelling value, combined with a shopping experience that makes it easy to choose Lowe's.

I want to again thank our merchants, our MST associates, our inventory and supply chain teams, along with our vendor partners for their execution, focus, and commitment to serving our customers and driving results. With that, I'll now turn the call over to Quonta.

Quonta Vance:Thanks, Bill, and good morning, everyone. I'm excited to join you today in my new role leading our stores organization. I've been in this role since the beginning of September, and it's been an honor to take over from my longtime friend and colleague, Joe McFarland. Over the past eight years, Joe has done an incredible job of transforming Lowe's into one of the best-executing retailers in the world. I also want to thank Joe for his partnership throughout this transition. I appreciate the strong foundation he and our stores have built. Turning to our third quarter performance. Let me start with Pro, where we delivered another quarter of strong growth, driven by our core small and medium-sized Pro customer.

We're seeing these Pros respond to the values we're creating, particularly through fulfillment and loyalty. As I saw up close in my prior role, time is money for the Pro. Every trip they can avoid gives them more time on the job site. That's why same-day fulfillment is such an important part of our value proposition for our Pro loyalty customers. When they need something to keep a job moving, we can get it to them quickly. During the quarter, our Pro savings days provided additional volume savings on products Pros use every day, including such items as cleaning, paint essentials, power tools, and accessories.

Together, these offers help us deliver more value, deepen relationships with existing Pro customers, and capture more of their spend. In our most recent survey, our core Pro customer reported steady backlogs and a consistent trend of smaller projects as repair and maintenance continues to be the dominant occasion. Pros expressed stable confidence levels, signaling that they remain optimistic about their ability to stay busy. Switching gears to home services. Strong execution drove another quarter of growth, our 10th straight. We continue to see strength in replacement categories where customers often have an immediate need and are looking for a trusted partner who can make the process easier.

We continue to streamline this customer journey by adding scheduling to the point of sale. Customers can now select their installation date when they make their purchase, simplifying the journey and giving them greater certainty as it relates to when their project will be completed. You will hear more about these developments and the improved customer experience in a few weeks at our Analyst and Investor Conference as we lay out our path for future growth. Across our stores, we're also delivering enhanced customer service for both the DIY and Pro customers while advancing our Perpetual Productivity Improvement initiatives. We will also discuss some of these specific initiatives in more detail at our December Analyst and Investor Conference.

In closing, to all of our store associates and leaders, thank you for the way you show up every day for our customers and for one another. I'm excited about the opportunity ahead, and I'm honored to lead this team. With that, I'll turn the call over to Brandon.

Brandon Sink:Thank you, Quonta, and good morning. In Q3, we delivered better-than-expected sales and earnings, reflecting strong execution across the business despite macroeconomic pressures. We saw continued momentum across several of our strategic growth areas while maintaining our focus on productivity, disciplined cost management, and investing for long-term growth. Beginning with our third quarter results, we generated GAAP diluted earnings per share of $2.98. In the quarter, we recognized $96 million in pre-tax non-GAAP charges from acquisition-related intangible asset amortization. Excluding these impacts, we delivered adjusted diluted earnings per share of $3.10. My comments from this point forward will include certain non-GAAP comparisons that exclude the impact of non-GAAP charges where applicable.

Sales for the third quarter were $22.8 billion, up 9.3% from the third quarter of last year. Comparable sales increased 1.8%, with August up 0.3%, September up 2.9%, and October up 2%. Please note that the shift in timing of Labor Day pressured August by approximately 150 basis points and benefited September by a similar amount. As Marvin and Bill discussed, we continue to see strong performance across several of our strategic growth areas, including Pro, online, and home services. We also saw strong performance in appliances and power equipment, driven by our assortment, value, and fulfillment capabilities, with power equipment also benefiting from strong Labor Day execution and an extended seasonal selling period.

Comparable average ticket increased 3.5%, while comparable transactions declined 1.7%. The increase in average ticket reflects mix into Pro and appliances, along with inflation in commodity-driven categories like lumber and electrical cable. Excluding commodity categories, like-for-like inflation was in line with our expectations. For the third quarter, gross margin was 32.9%, down 124 basis points versus prior year gross margin. Gross margin includes approximately 120 basis points from IEEPA tariff refunds this quarter, which drove $0.34 of adjusted diluted earnings per share. In the quarter, we reinvested about one-third of the refunds into actions to reinforce customer value. We expect to reinvest the remainder of the tariff refunds in Q4.

Gross margin was also impacted by dilution from the FBM acquisition, in line with our expectations. Importantly, we have now fully cycled that impact following the acquisition's close at the end of Q3 last year. We saw elevated fuel and transportation costs, which represented approximately 30 basis points of pressure, along with a combination of product mix and tariff reinvestments. SG&A was 19% of sales, leveraging 55 basis points versus prior year adjusted SG&A, in line with our expectations. Adjusted operating margin was 11.7%, down 67 basis points versus prior year adjusted operating margin.

Our PPI initiatives, spanning merchandising, stores, supply chain, and our corporate functions, continued to deliver meaningful productivity in the quarter, helping us manage these external cost pressures while continuing to invest in the business. The effective tax rate was 24.5%. Inventory ended the third quarter at $18.3 billion, up $1.1 billion versus prior year, driven by the normalization of prior year tariff-related timing disruptions and investments to support in-stock levels. We remain focused on improving inventory productivity while ensuring we have the right products available for our customers. Moving to capital allocation. in Q3, we generated $1.1 billion in free cash flow, and capital expenditures totaled $601 million as we continued to invest in our strategic growth priorities.

We paid $701 million in dividends at $1.25 per share, reinforcing our commitment to returning capital to shareholders and reaffirming our status as both a Dividend Aristocrat and a Dividend King. We finished the quarter with adjusted debt to EBITDA of approximately 3.0 times, as we continue to progress towards our 2.75x leverage ratio target, which we expect to achieve in 2027. We ended Q3 with $3.4 billion of cash and cash equivalents and delivered return on invested capital of 22.9%. Turning now to our financial outlook. Today, we are updating our full year 2026 outlook to reflect our third quarter results, as well as the current demand trends and cost pressures we're seeing across the business.

Based on this, we now expect sales of approximately $92.5 billion, with comparable sales up approximately 0.5%. We expect adjusted operating margin of approximately 11.5% and full year adjusted diluted earnings per share of approximately $12.25. We expect capital expenditures of up to $2.5 billion. For the fourth quarter, we expect comp sales to be slightly positive. Please keep in mind that we are cycling approximately 50 basis points of storm-related benefit from Q4 last year. This was concentrated entirely in January, which will create an approximately 200 basis points comp sales headwind for the month. Excluding that impact, our underlying consumer demand assumption is generally consistent with Q3.

In the fourth quarter, we expect to reinvest the remaining two-thirds of the Q3 tariff refunds into initiatives focused on our customer value proposition. Our priority is to put these dollars back to work for our customers, helping make their home improvement projects more affordable while building loyalty to Lowe's. In a few weeks, at our Analyst and Investor Conference, we look forward to sharing more about the growth opportunities we see across Lowe's and how we expect that growth to translate through our longer-term financial model. in the meantime, we're focused on delivering strong execution through the important holiday season and on driving profitable sales growth and taking market share while maintaining discipline across the business.

With that, we are now ready to take your questions.

Operator:Thank you. We are now ready for questions. If you would like to ask a question, press star then one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star two. In order to allow questions for as many individuals as possible, please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. Our first question today is from the line of Chris Horvers with JPMorgan. Please proceed with your question.

Chris Horvers:Thanks, and good morning, everybody. Brandon, I want to dovetail on that, your underlying trend comment a little bit. How much do you think weather benefited you during the quarter? Was that exclusive to September? Then as you think about October and looking forward, did you see any election noise that maybe diminished what was overall a pretty strong month in October?

Brandon Sink:Hey, Chris. When we look overall at the shape of the quarter, pretty even as we looked at August, September, October. Weather overall, I would say, was pretty much a non-story. We have not had a named storm of significance here the last couple of years. We did see a little bit of a bump in October for the extended selling season period with a little bit warmer October benefiting some of our outdoor categories. So really not much to speak of in Q3. Then I had in my remarks, just as we look ahead to Q4, we are cycling Winter Storm Fern.

It was 50 basis points on the quarter expected that we will be cycling for Q4 and 200 basis points in January. Outside of that, no real noise around the election, and excited about the exit rate, the performance for Q3, the trajectory, and feel really good about how we are trending into Q4.

Chris Horvers:You kNOW, as you think about 2027, I know we will get a lot at the Analyst Day, but I think there is. You have in the bootcamp, you sit there and you say, look, replacement cycles persist and maybe even accelerate. There is going to be a little bit more inflation. Life goes on. People stay in place and remodel. But then you have the impact of higher rates. Just broad strokes, if you are exiting the back half of the year at around a sort of a one-ish underlying trend, net of weather impacts, does that accelerate into next year given the positive factors?

Or do you think that it actually decelerates next year given how maybe there is an impact, a lagged impact on rates on demand? Thank you.

Marvin Ellison:Chris, this is Marvin. I think the simple response would be it is too early to determine all the specifics of that. What we intend to do at the Analyst and Investor Conference in December is lay out a very specific strategy of how we can grow irrespective of the macro environment. We simply believe because of the fragmented total addressable market that is the U.S. home improvement environment, that there is a lot of market share out there that we can go and get. We have some very specific initiatives that we are going to lay out and discuss in December that will reinforce our confidence that we can make that happen.

We look forward to discussing that in the next couple of weeks.

Chris Horvers:Thanks. Have a great holiday season.

Marvin Ellison:Thanks, Chris.

Operator:Our next questions are from the line of Steven Zaccone with Citi. Please proceed with your questions.

Steven Zaccone:Hey, good morning. Thanks very much for taking my question. Could I ask for a little bit more detail on the tariff reinvestment? Maybe how should we think about that in terms of pricing, any aspect of promotions in the fourth quarter? Just help us understand how you're thinking about that reimbursement as we turn to 4Q.

Brandon Sink:Yeah. Hey, Steve. This is Brandon. As we mentioned, we had the refund of approximately $250 million that we recognized in Q3. We have invested and did invest one-third of that refund in Q3, and that was largely in initiatives to reinforce our customer value proposition, remain competitive in the market. Couple examples I'll throw out is just supporting tier one promo events, investing in our loyalty ecosystem, continuing to lean in to enhance fulfillment, specifically within our online platform, and that gives our members additional benefits, value. We're really seeing them respond to that. The remaining two-thirds is where we expect to invest in Q4. Again, that's focused again in those same areas, reinforcing that customer value proposition.

So really, it's net neutral on the year. The timing of the refunds and the associated reinvestments is really just leading to the lumpiness between quarters, and that's what we're seeing with the Q3 actual results and what's expected for Q4.

Steven Zaccone:Okay. I wanted to follow up with a question about the underlying trend in the business, because you had stronger results overall from a comp perspective, but there was less breadth in terms of the categories. When you think about the building blocks of customer engagement, some of these category performance details, have you seen changes from a Pro or DIY perspective that is noteworthy to call out?

Marvin Ellison:Steven, this is Marvin. I will take that, and then I will let Bill provide some more category specifics. As we said in the prepared comments, when we think about the business performance, we saw strength across Pro, and as Quonta said, specific to small to medium Pro, we are gaining share with that specific cohort of the Pro business. Appliances was a huge win for us, and we just simply believe that the best-in-class fulfillment ecosystem and the assortment that we have is incomparable in the U.S.

As Bill mentioned, we are the only retailer in the U.S. that has a large variety of products that we can deliver and install and hook up same day and next day in virtually every zip code. In fact, our appliance comp was the largest we have seen in five years, and that says a lot when you think about the pressure that the DIY consumer is under. As Quonta mentioned, our home services business is strong as well. We had other strength across the business. I will hand over to Bill, and he can provide a little bit more context.

Bill Boltz:Yeah, Steve. When we look at Q3, as I said in my prepared remarks, we have had some strength and continued strength across our Pro businesses. Rough plumbing is a great example. Six-plus quarters of positive comps in the rough plumbing business, really widespread from the discretionary areas of HVAC all the way to water heaters and that repair and maintenance type of product. When we look at appliances, as Marvin just mentioned, we had our eighth consecutive quarter of positive comp growth in appliances. Q3 was our strongest comp since 2021, and so there is some really just great momentum within the appliance business.

Just a reminder to the group, 100,000 appliances break every day, and I think our model, I know our model is there to stand tall to be able to deliver same day, next day, and handle that duress customer. Then just a little more color across some of the categories. There is still pressure in these discretionary areas like kitchens, like flooring, but then when you dig deeper into some of the seasonal areas, we saw strength in patio furniture in Q3. We saw strength across outdoor power, as I mentioned in my prepared remarks, really across all segments. So whether that is generators, riding mowers because of the extended season, walk-behind mowers.

But you are also seeing consumers respond to what happened last year in January with Winter Storm Fern, so they are now preparing for that winter season, and so we saw some early response for snowblowers. Both segments of both battery and gas segments did very well. Then when you dig into some of the other businesses and look a little deeper, like in the garden area, for example, strength across the outdoor project, landscape, fertilizer, landscape mulch, those types of hardscapes were strong. And then when we look into that tools and hardware business, which is supporting this repair and maintenance project, fastening, storage, those key categories continue to perform well and have performed well for a long time.

So, we are pleased with kind of the broad-based breadth of the business that was performing and the strength of what was performing. And early on in Q4, we are seeing some of that with the milder weather. We are seeing some of those outdoor projects continue to get done, both on the Pro side as well as the DIY side.

Steven Zaccone:Great. Thanks for all that detail.

Operator:Our next question is from the line of Kate McShane with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed with your questions.

Kate McShane:Hi, good morning. Thanks for taking our question. We had one question when it came to margin for Q4, just how you are balancing some of that tariff refund with any kind of offset with regards to higher freight costs. Could you also please talk to the performance of the marketplace during the quarter? Thank you.

Brandon Sink:Hey, Kate. This is Brandon. As it relates to Q4 margin, it is really just a few themes. I have already spoken to the tariff reinvestment. About two-thirds of what we recognized in Q3 will be reinvested in Q4. You mentioned the higher fuel transportation. That definitely has been an ongoing pressure that we have spoken to throughout the year. We have actually seen that accelerate as we moved here through Q3 relative to our earlier guide in August. Diesel prices, as we stand here today, are right around $6. So, that is up about 15% overall versus what we realized in Q2.

So trying to continue to manage that, balance that, and we are reflecting that into our Q4 guide. The last piece is just as it relates to mix into different margin profile categories. You just heard Bill speak to the strength that we are seeing specifically in appliances. OPE did a double-digit comp in Q3, and we are looking ahead there to similar run rates. So, increased adoption of fulfillment options online and trying to take all that into consideration, and that is what is reflected in the Q4. As it relates to the marketplace question, Kate, we actually have a really strong update for that in Q4. Excited to share more with you.

Obviously seeing great growth in our online business. As a reminder, the marketplace is reflected there on a net commission basis, so we will start to share more color and more information there in December and as we lap into 2027.

Marvin Ellison:Kate, this is Marvin. Specifically to the online performance, we felt early on that marketplace was a great addition to the digital strategy. It gives us an opportunity to offer customers value and luxury without adding inventory. We have some advancements that Brandon mentioned that we are going to be sharing in a little bit more detail and color. We wanted to give our marketplace strategy a full year of operation before we start to speak specifically on the components of it, the financial performance, and what we are seeing and projecting.

We will share that in some detail in December, but just to reinforce what we said about the online performance, we had growth of 17.4%, fifth straight quarter of double-digit growth, third straight quarter of growth over 15%, strength across Pro, DIY, improved traffic and conversion, and also the enhancements that we made in our fulfillment options are absolutely working, and we have another update coming on that as well in December, and marketplace is obviously a component of that, and again, we will be more specific and share that with you at the Analyst and Investor Conference in December.

Kate McShane:Thank you.

Brandon Sink:Thank you, Kate.

Operator:Our next questions are from the line of Michael Lasser with UBS. Please proceed with your questions.

Michael Lasser:Good morning. Thank you so much for taking my question. You raised your full-year sales guidance by about $500 million, yet you lowered your operating margin outlook by about 10 basis points or so. Was that entirely due to the fuel pressure that you referenced, or are there other factors? Would you expect to be able to recover the pressure in 2027 such that you will be operating from a normalized margin base next year? Then I have a quick follow-up.

Brandon Sink:Yeah. Hey, Michael. You mentioned the top line. Again, very pleased with the trajectory. If I go back to August, our implied guide for top line was roughly flat. We exceeded that with a +1.8%. Looking now into Q4, we had implied back in August down one. That is roughly flat as of now. So continue to be really pleased with the performance. Bill went into some of the details around where we are seeing momentum. As it relates to the margin guide and the update, it is really three themes, and I've already hit them.

It is the tariff refund and the expected reinvestment, the majority of that going into Q4, and that is gonna be neutral on the year. Elevated fuel and transportation costs, there is gonna be, as you referenced there, Michael, some wrap pressure in the next year, and then the mix of sales into some of these lower margin profile businesses and categories, appliances and OPE as an example. So that is what we have reflected in our guide. That is in the 11.5% for the year. As it relates to 2027, jump off points, wrap pressure, we are focused right now on landing the 2026 guide.

We have a, what I believe is a really nice strong message in 2027 here coming up in December, and that is going to include our views on 2027, as well as sales margin, what the trajectory looks like there.

Marvin Ellison:Michael, this is Marvin. The only thing I'll add to that is, we are going to share some PPI initiatives. You heard Quonta earlier talk about some of the really specific successes we have had in the store operations area of the business. As you have heard us say in the past, PPI is now an enterprise-wide focus for the company. As we deal with some of these unique pressures, like fuel, which is unprecedented, that just means that we are going to be more aggressive in going after these Perpetual Productivity Improvement initiatives. We are going to share some of those in December.

We have some areas that is supported by technology that we are very excited about, that we have not really talked about publicly, that we will share.
